subject: Re: Procurement path & PO constraints — next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Lisa Chang <lisa.chang@acme.com>, Tom Erickson <tom.erickson@acme.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Mar 2026 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: procurement next steps and commercial path

Hi Lisa / Tom —

Thanks again for taking the call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment on the procurement path: 

- Discovery recap: Acme is evaluating Redwood for customer-facing summary generation across product lines (primary latency and data isolation requirements called out).
- Commercial path options we discussed: purchase order (PO) via AP, payment card on file (corporate card), or marketplace (AWS/GC) listing.
- Open constraints from your side: you mentioned existing policies that restrict POs for SaaS vendors or require prepayment for new vendors — can you confirm the exact blocker?

Next steps / asks from Acme:
1) Confirm whether Acme can issue a PO (net terms) or if card/prepay is required.
2) If PO is allowed, confirm procurement docs and any preferred contract language.
3) If PO is not permitted, confirm whether prepay or marketplace purchase would work.

I've attached our pricing proposal and a draft SOW for reference (Redwood_PRICING_PROPOSAL.pdf, Redwood_SOW_draft.pdf).

If it helps, we can also propose an exception path (partial prepay or card on file with spend threshold) — happy to escalate internally.

Thanks,

Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0198

From: Lisa Chang <lisa.chang@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Erickson <tom.erickson@acme.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Mar 2026 10:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: procurement next steps and commercial path

Hi Marissa —

Thanks for the clear recap. To confirm Acme's procurement constraints:

- We do not issue POs for SaaS vendors under $50k ARR without Finance review — our policy is to centralize payments for new SaaS vendors through prepayment or marketplace purchases where possible.
- We cannot complete marketplace purchases for products that require us to transfer customer data outside our tenancy (given your hosting details).
- Our preferred path would be a prepay invoice (Finance will issue payment up front) or corporate card payment if the vendor supports it.

Action items for Redwood: please provide (a) a draft contract/SOW showing prepay terms you can accept, and (b) confirmation on whether Redwood can accept card on file for monthly billing. If neither is possible, we'll need to loop in Finance for an exception.

Thanks —
Lisa Chang
Senior Procurement Manager
Acme Industrial
lisa.chang@acme.com

Hi Lisa —

Thanks for the clarity. Looping in Ben (Sales Ops / Commercial) and Dev (Solutions) to outline feasible commercial paths from our side.

Ben / Dev — Acme's policy: no PO for vendors <$50k without Finance review, marketplace not viable due to tenancy/data constraints. They prefer either:

- Prepay (Finance issues an upfront payment for an agreed term), or
- Card on file (monthly billing), or
- Exception for a PO if Redwood accepts limited net terms and Finance approves.

Could you confirm which options we can offer and any minimums or prepay scheduling required? I've attached the draft SOW and pricing. If we need a short exception playbook (e.g., 30% upfront, remainder net 30), please propose language we can share with Acme Finance.

Thanks —
Marissa

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Procurement path & PO constraints — exception options

Hi Lisa / Marissa —

Appreciate the details. From Sales Ops / Commercial here's what we can offer for Acme: 

1) Prepay: We can accept an upfront payment for 6 months or 12 months. Standard is 30% upfront + net 30 on the balance for bespoke deals, but for a first-time vendor we can accept 100% prepay for the term you prefer.

2) Card on file: We can support card-on-file monthly billing. For corporate card payments, Finance often requests a spend threshold. If Acme expects < $50k ARR in year one, card on file monthly billing is the cleanest path and we can avoid PO paperwork.

3) PO exception: If Acme requires a PO, we can scope a short exception: 30% prepay + remaining on net 30 after delivery milestones. This requires Sales Ops sign-off; I can get approval if Acme's legal signs the standard SOW and we get a counter-signed contract within 10 business days.

Because marketplace purchase is blocked by tenancy concerns, the recommended path is either full prepay for the initial term or card on file. Please confirm which Acme prefers and I'll generate the appropriate invoice/terms.

HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/ACME-12345 — I'll add the chosen billing path to the deal and kick off Sales Ops for approvals if needed.

Best,
Ben Carter
Sales Operations
Redwood Inference
ben@redwood.com
